headline: Home Ministry task force to replace all city dustbins with 'anti-habit' sensors that dispense harsh judgment
body:
Q: The Home Ministry's new initiative aims to wipe out public littering by 2029 with the same intensity as narcotics control. How exactly do these new 'moral-correction' bins function?

A: It’s quite simple. We’ve replaced standard containers with AI-powered kiosks that monitor your intent. If you approach a bin holding a plastic wrapper, the sensor detects if you’re discarding it with 'civic indifference.' If it senses a lack of remorse, it immediately plays a loud, pre-recorded voice note of your mother asking why you were raised this way.

Q: Is the goal really just cleanliness, or is there a broader social strategy at play here?

A: We’re moving beyond just cleaning streets; we’re eradicating the very impulse to litter. By 2029, our data suggests that the sheer psychological weight of public shaming will make the concept of 'trash' obsolete. We are treating littering with the same zero-tolerance, high-stakes tactical approach one would use to dismantle a complex underground distribution network.

Q: Some residents have complained that being lectured by a bin while trying to dispose of a mango peel is excessive.

A: That’s exactly the kind of weakness we’re targeting. If you can’t handle a fifteen-second lecture from a plastic receptacle about your personal contribution to national entropy, how can we expect you to commit to a clean, drug-free, and litter-free nation by 2029? It’s about building character through inconvenience.
caption: New smart bins are here to make sure your trash disposal comes with a side of existential dread. Don't let your garbage pile up, or the sensors will start reciting your search history. #SwachhBharat #SmartCity #ZeroTolerance #CivicDuty (satire)
igHook: Would you still throw your wrapper away if the dustbin knew your secrets?
